title: Current fluctuations of diffusive systems with a battery
abstract: For a diffusive system on a ring, with a battery at the origin, we use the macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT) to obtain the large deviation function of the current. In the case of non-interacting particles, the predictions of the MFT agree with the result of a direct exact microscopic calculation. To our surprise, the large deviation function of non-interacting particles with a battery has the same form as for the Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process (SSEP) with open boundary conditions. For the SSEP on a ring with a battery, the predictions of the MFT seem to agree with the results of long Monte Carlo simulations, although much longer simulations would be needed to better test the validity of these predictions.
summary: This work analyzes current fluctuations in diffusive systems on a ring containing a battery, using Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory. The authors find a surprising mathematical equivalence between the fluctuation statistics of non-interacting particles and those of the SSEP under certain conditions. The research provides detailed comparisons between theoretical predictions and long-time numerical simulations for these non-equilibrium transport phenomena.
main_problem: The paper investigates the large deviation function and fluctuation statistics of the current in diffusive systems subjected to a localized non-conservative force (a battery).
main_result: The large deviation function for non-interacting particles on a ring surprisingly matches the form found for the Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process (SSEP) with open boundary conditions.
method: The authors employ Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (MFT) for analytical predictions and complement this with direct exact microscopic calculations and extensive Monte Carlo simulations.
model_or_system: The system is a diffusive particle model on a ring containing a battery at the origin. Models include non-interacting particles and the SSEP, which are analyzed under steady-state conditions.
key_observables: Large deviation function of the current, average occupations, density profiles, and the second cumulant of the integrated current.
important_parameters: The particle density ($ ar{ho}$), the battery strength ($G, H$), and the system size ($L$) are key parameters explored across different regimes.
main_assumptions: MFT relies on assumptions about the optimal profile being time-independent, and the analysis compares results derived from different theoretical limits (e.g., non-interacting vs. SSEP).
figures_summary: Figures compare the average current and the second cumulant of the current (MC vs. MFT) as a function of density, notably highlighting a specific value of 1/3 at half-filling for the SSEP.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the framework using MFT for current fluctuations, then deriving specific results for non-interacting particles, and finally comparing these findings and the second cumulant analysis for the SSEP against long Monte Carlo simulations.
why_interesting: The study bridges classical non-equilibrium statistical mechanics (MFT) with particle exclusion processes (SSEP), providing deep insights into how boundary conditions and particle interactions affect current fluctuations in mesoscopic systems.

There is one special link (red, thick) between sites L and 1, with transfer rate G from site L to site 1, and trans- fer rate H ≤G from site 1 to site L. This special link plays the role of a battery.
